applies_to: Alber BDSU battery monitoring systems (strings and cells).
summary: The Alber BDSU battery monitoring reports battery string and cell data through a Liebert IntelliSlot card: string voltage, current and temperatures, cell voltages, temperatures and resistance, and alarm thresholds. Object names for string and cell points are generated at runtime from the BDSU configuration.
notes: Tables 5.194, 5.195, 5.196, pdf pages 2287-2306 of the 2024 guide (printed page numbers are 4 lower).
Object names are Vertiv data IDs (e.g. 5331_1); the description holds the guide's data label. Labels repeated for different sensors or circuits get the group name in brackets.
Most temperature objects come in pairs: a °C object and a °F object (name ending _deg_F), usually at instance + 10000.
String and cell object names contain a <SeeDnldMap> placeholder that the card fills at runtime; download BACnetDataMap.txt from the Unity card for the real names.

source.title: Liebert IntelliSlot Modbus/BACnet Reference Guide (Modbus RTU and TCP, BACnet MSTP and IP)

integration.summary: Fit a Liebert IntelliSlot BACnet card (IS-UNITY-DP for BACnet IP or MS/TP), give it a unique device instance and let it discover the equipment; the objects are then created automatically. Map the status, main measurements and event objects for monitoring.
setup: The card needs a unique Device Instance Number; the device object represents the card, not the unit.
The cards have no BBMD; IS-UNITY-DP and IS-IPBML support foreign device registration (BBMD address and time-to-live).
IS-UNITY-DP adds BACnet MS/TP; IS-WEBADPT and IS-IPBML are BACnet IP only. Check the compatibility table (guide section 1.1.3) for the card your unit supports.
gotchas: Vertiv asks for no more than about two writes and two reads per second on average; do not rewrite setpoints continuously.
No segmented responses: large ReadPropertyMultiple requests can fail, so split them.
Only data the managed unit actually has is created on the card, so object counts vary by model and options.
